name: Starter: Haitian Creole
about: Haitian Creole in real, everyday sentences, with each one's words in Creole order.

words.èske: is it that (starts a yes-or-no question)
words.la: the (la, a, an, lan, nan, after the noun)
words.ye: is (at the end of a question)
words.yo: they; after a noun: the ones, more than one

items.text: Yon te ak yon dlo, tanpri.
items.means: A tea and a water, please.
wrong: Te yon ak dlo yon, tanpri.
Yon te ak dlo yon, tanpri.

items.text: Bonjou! Mwen kontan fè konesans ou.
wrong: Bonjou! Mwen se kontan fè konesans ou.
Bonjou! Mwen kontan fè ou konesans.
Èske ou se gen yon kle?

items.text: Mwen gen yon frè ak yon sè.
items.means: I have a brother and a sister.
wrong: Mwen se gen yon frè ak yon sè.
Mwen gen frè yon ak sè yon.

items.text: Eskize mwen, ki kote twalèt la ye?

wrong: Eskize mwen, ki kote la twalèt ye?
Eskize mwen, ki kote twalèt la se?

items.means: Excuse me, how much is it?
I speak a little Haitian Creole.

Mwen rete nan ti yon kay.

items.text: Manman mwen ale nan vil la.
items.means: My mother goes to the city.
wrong: Manman mwen se ale nan vil la.
Manman mwen ale nan la vil.

items.text: Eskize mwen, ki kote estasyon tren an ye?
items.means: Excuse me, where is the train station?
wrong: Eskize mwen, ki kote an estasyon tren ye?
Eskize mwen, ki kote estasyon tren an se?
Mwen se dwe ale kounye a.
Mwen dwe se ale kounye a.

items.text: Mwen pa ka ale jodi a.
wrong: Mwen pa se ka ale jodi a.
Mwen pa ale ka jodi a.

items.text: Demen mwen ale nan vil la.
items.means: Tomorrow I go to the city.
wrong: Demen mwen se ale nan vil la.
Demen mwen ale nan la vil.

items.text: M gen yon frè ak yon sè.
items.means: I have a brother and a sister.
wrong: M se yon frè ak yon sè.

items.text: Timoun yo ap jwe nan lakou a.
items.means: The children are playing in the yard.
wrong: Timoun yo jwe nan lakou a.
Yo timoun ap jwe nan lakou a.

items.means: The keys are on the table.

items.text: Pa gen lèt nan frijidè a.
items.means: There's no milk in the fridge.
wrong: Pa se lèt nan frijidè a.
Pa gen lèt sou frijidè a.

items.text: Manman m ap fè manje lakay.
items.means: My mom is cooking at home.

items.text: Nou rete nan sant vil la.
items.means: We live in the city center.
wrong: Nou rete sou sant vil la.

items.means: The books are on the shelf.

wrong: Chak maten mwen se bwè kafe.

wrong: Mwen se vle yon kafe ak lèt.
Mwen vle kafe yon ak lèt.

items.text: Èske m ka peye ak kat?
wrong: Èske m ka se peye ak kat?

items.text: Yè nou te manje nan yon restoran.
items.means: Yesterday we ate at a restaurant.
wrong: Yè nou pral manje nan yon restoran.

items.text: Pa t gen pen nan boutik la.
items.means: There was no bread at the store.
wrong: Pa pral gen pen nan boutik la.

items.means: I want to drink a juice.

items.text: Ban m yon vè dlo, tanpri.
items.means: Give me a glass of water, please.
wrong: Ban li yon vè dlo, tanpri.

items.text: Ki kote estasyon otobis la ye?
wrong: Ki kote estasyon otobis la se?

items.text: Ki lè otobis la ap rive?
wrong: Ki kote otobis la ap rive?

items.text: Èske gen yon bank toupre isit la?
items.means: Is there a bank near here?
wrong: Èske se yon bank toupre isit la?

items.text: Demen m pral nan ayewopò a.
items.means: Tomorrow I'm going to the airport.
wrong: Demen m te nan ayewopò a.

items.text: Yè m te achte yon pè soulye nèf.
items.means: Yesterday I bought a pair of new shoes.
wrong: Yè m pral achte yon pè soulye nèf.

items.means: The pharmacy is near the bank.

wrong: Èske ou ka se ede m?

items.means: Last year we were in Cap-Haïtien.

items.text: N ap al sinema ak zanmi m.
items.means: We're going to the movies with my friend.
wrong: N ap al sinema ak m zanmi.

concept.line: mwen (I, me), ou (you), li (he, she, it, him, her), nou (we, us, you all) and yo (they, them) often shorten to m, w, l, n and y where the sounds around them allow: M grangou (I hungry), M ap rele w (I will call you).

A verb never takes se as an English is, bare or after ka or pral; with no time marker, a state can be true now, an action a habit, or the time around it can make it past: Mwen vle dlo (I want water), Mwen travay chak jou (I work every day), Yè mwen achte pen (yesterday I bought bread).

words.means: am, is, are (linking the subject to a noun or noun phrase)

concept.line: My and your come after the noun, as the pronoun: liv mwen (book my), manman m (mother my), kay li (house his).

words.means: am, is, are (used after the subject in questions such as “where …?” and “how …?”)

concept.line: The singular the follows the whole noun phrase and takes one of five forms, by the sounds before it: liv la (book the), bato a (boat the), kay nou an (house our the), machin nan (car the), bank lan (bank the).
pa goes before the verb and before ap, te and pral: M pa konnen (I not know), Li pa t vini (she not did come).

words.means: marks an ongoing action (am/is/are …-ing); can also mark future action

concept.line: A question word starts the question: Ki kote ou rete?
